title: Thinking Deeper in Gemini — Jack Rae, Google DeepMind

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The primary object is the model itself: test-time compute as a new scaling paradigm, thinking as intrinsic model behavior trained via RL, and emergent reasoning capabilities—not a serving system or post-training recipe. Gemini is a general-purpose foundation model discussed without a specific application vertical. Thinking is trained via RL in post-training and operates at inference time through dynamic compute allocation and thinking budgets. summary: Jack Rae frames AI progress as a cycle of identifying fundamental intelligence bottlenecks and solving them. He traces this history: Claude Shannon's 1948 bigram language model was limited by small data and elementary statistics; Google's 2000s-era n-gram models over trillions of tokens were bottlenecked by short context length due to exponential storage costs; 2010s recurrent neural networks solved context compression but introduced lossy fixed-size state representations; attention mechanisms and transformers resolved this by retaining all past embeddings and aggregating on the fly. The current bottleneck is test-time compute: modern LLMs apply a fixed amount of computation between request and response. Thinking in Gemini addresses this by inserting an iterative thinking stage where the model emits additional text before committing to a final answer, enabling potentially tens of thousands of additional computation iterations. This loop is dynamic—the model learns how many iterations to apply. Training uses reinforcement learning with vague correctness signals, which surprisingly produced emergent behaviors like hypothesis testing, self-correction, problem decomposition, exploring multiple solutions, drafting modular code, intermediate calculations, and tool use. Thinking stacks multiplicatively on pre-training and post-training scaling paradigms, accelerating overall model improvement. Empirically, test-time scaling works: Gemini 2.5 Pro launched with thinking shows improved reasoning over prior December models. Thinking also introduces a continuous quality-cost budget—a granular slider replacing the old discrete choice of model sizes—now available in Flash and Pro 2.5 series. Looking ahead, Rae highlights improving reasoning efficiency (addressing model overthinking), Deep Think mode (a high-budget asynchronous thinking mode built on 2.5 Pro using deeper and parallel chains of thought, improving USA Math Olympiad performance from negligible to 50th percentile with 2.5 Pro and 65th percentile with Deep Think), and excitement about open-ended coding tasks where models can replicate complex systems like DeepMind's DQN Atari emulator in minutes. His long-term vision draws on Ramanujan, who derived vast mathematics from a single textbook—aiming for models that are incredibly data-efficient and can sustain millions of inference tokens of deep contemplation to push the frontier of human understanding.

sections.title: Introduction and Talk Overview
sections.summary: Jack Rae introduces himself as tech lead of thinking within Gemini and outlines a three-stage talk: research motivation for thinking as an intelligence bottleneck solution, practical explanation of what thinking is in Gemini for developers, and what's next. Technical difficulties with slides occur briefly.

sections.title: Intelligence Bottlenecks Through History
sections.summary: Rae traces AI progress as identifying and solving bottlenecks: Shannon's 1948 bigram model (limited by data and statistics), Google's 2000s n-gram models (limited by short context due to exponential storage costs), 2010s RNNs (limited by lossy fixed-size state), and attention/transformers (solved by retaining all past embeddings). Each bottleneck solution enabled a step-change in capability.

sections.title: Test-Time Compute Bottleneck and Thinking in Gemini
sections.summary: The current 2024 bottleneck is that LLMs apply fixed test-time compute regardless of problem difficulty. Thinking in Gemini inserts an iterative loop before the final answer, enabling dynamic compute allocation across potentially tens of thousands of iterations. Trained via reinforcement learning with only correctness signals, the model develops emergent strategies: hypothesis testing, self-correction, problem decomposition, multi-solution exploration, modular code drafting, intermediate calculations, and tool use.

sections.title: Developer Benefits and Performance Scaling
sections.summary: Thinking drives more capable models and stacks multiplicatively on pre-training and post-training scaling paradigms, accelerating overall model improvement. Reasoning performance across math, code, and science tracks with log-scale increases in test-time compute. Recent Gemini 2.5 Pro launches show improved reasoning performance corresponding to increased test-time compute allocation.

sections.title: Thinking Budgets and Steerability
sections.summary: Test-time scaling works empirically, as shown by comparing a December model without thinking to Gemini 2.5 Pro with thinking. Thinking introduces a continuous quality-cost budget replacing the old discrete choice of model sizes, giving developers a granular slider for capability versus cost. Thinking budgets are launched in Gemini 2.5 Flash and Pro series.

sections.title: What's Next: Efficiency, Deep Think, and Future Vision
sections.summary: Rae outlines future directions: improving reasoning quality, making thinking efficient and adaptive (addressing model overthinking), and Deep Think mode—a high-budget asynchronous thinking mode built on 2.5 Pro using deeper and parallel chains of thought. Deep Think improves USA Math Olympiad performance from negligible (January SOTA) to 50th percentile (2.5 Pro) to 65th percentile (Deep Think). He shares excitement about open-ended vibecoding tasks, citing colleagues who replicated DeepMind's DQN paper and Atari emulator in minutes. His long-term vision invokes Ramanujan—models that are incredibly data-efficient, deriving vast knowledge from small inputs over millions of inference tokens.

demonstrations: Historical artifact showing a model using thinking tokens to pose a hypothesis, test it, reject it when the formula doesn't hold, and try an alternative approach on an integer prediction problem
Video animation of a USA Math Olympiad algebra problem showing multiple iterative proof ideas (proof by contradiction, Rolle's theorem, Newton's inequalities) being explored and integrated
Colleagues vibecoded DeepMind's original DQN paper training setup, algorithm, and an Atari emulator using Gemini in minutes—a task that previously took months
limitations: Claude Shannon could not scale his bigram model due to needing digitalization of human knowledge and modern computing
N-gram language models restricted to short context due to exponential storage cost with context length
RNNs had lossy representation of context due to fixed-size state
Simply making models larger does not provide the dynamic range users want for very hard tasks
Models can overthink on tasks, and improving efficiency of thinking is an ongoing area of research
